previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of COPD, chronic pain from prior trauma, alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was admitted for cough and alcohol intoxication. He initially expressed willingness to engage in treatment and rehab but became agitated and demanded opioid pain medication. When this was not provided due to safety concerns, he chose to leave against medical advice within an hour of admission. He did not receive treatment for COPD exacerbation or alcohol withdrawal, though breathing treatments provided some symptom relief. He was discharged alert and ambulatory with prescriptions for antibiotics, steroids, blood pressure medications, and vitamins, and urged to follow up and consider rehab. His chest X-ray showed no pneumonia, and blood cultures were negative.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, unspecified
Sedative, hypnotic or anxiolytic abuse, unspecified
Family history of malignant neoplasm of trachea, bronchus, and lung

is flattening of the diaphragms, suggesting chronic obstructive pulmonary
disease.  Bibasilar atelectasis is seen.  Additional right base patchy opacity
is seen, which could relate to atelectasis, although underlying infection or
aspiration may be present.  No large pleural effusion or pneumothorax is seen.
The cardiac silhouette is top normal.  The mediastinum is unremarkable.  Hilar
contours are stable.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Bibasilar opacities, likely due to atelectasis, increased right base
opacity may be due to atelectasis, although underlying infection or aspiration
is not excluded.
2.  COPD.
